papers.title: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Dose Exploration Study of CTI-1601 in Adult Subjects With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety and tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of subcutaneous (SC) administration of CTI-1601 over 28 days in subjects with Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA).

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy Study of A0001 in Subjects With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
This is a Phase 2a double-blind, placebo-controlled study with two dose levels of A0001 given twice daily for 28 days. Potential subjects will be screened first to determine eligibility, after which they will be randomized to receive either a high dose of A0001, a low dose of A0001 or placebo for 28 days.

Eligible subjects will return within 21 days of screening for the baseline visit and randomization to one of three potential treatments. The subjects will be required to take 3 capsules of study medication in the morning with a morning meal and 3 capsules of study medication at night with an

papers.title: FRDA Investigator Initiated Study (IIS) With Elamipretide
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, and activity of Elamipretide in treating vision loss in Friedreich Ataxia (FRDA).

papers.title: A Study of ASP2016 in Adults Who Have Heart Disease Associated With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary:
Friedreich Ataxia is a rare condition that causes damage to the nervous system and muscles. People with Friedreich Ataxia have difficulty walking, lose sensation in their arms and legs, and have slurred speech. It can also affect the heart and many people with Friedrich Ataxia develop serious heart problems. Friedreich Ataxia is a genetic condition which means a faulty gene is passed down through families. This type of gene therapy treats a genetic condition by providing a healthy copy of the gene.

At the time this study started, there was no approved treatment for heart problems in people wi

papers.title: Safety Study of Carbamylated Erythropoietin to Treat Patients With the Neurodegenerative Disorder Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The primary purpose of the study is to determine whether carbamylated erythropoietin is a safe treatment for patients who suffer from Friedreich's Ataxia.

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Vatiquinone for the Treatment of Participants With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the efficacy (using the modified Friedreich Ataxia Rating Scale \[mFARS\]) and safety of vatiquinone in participants with Friedreich ataxia (FA).

papers.title: Patient Reported Outcomes in Friedreich's Ataxia Patients After Withdrawal From Treatment With Idebenone (PROTI)
papers.summary:
This is a Phase IIIb Double-Blind, Randomised, Placebo-Controlled Study. The aim is to further investigate the effects of idebenone in patients with Friedreich's ataxia.

The objective of the PROTI study is to establish whether patients can correctly determine which treatment assignment (placebo or idebenone) they received during the randomised phase of the trial, and identify any potential changes on symptoms or activities.

papers.title: An Open-label Study of the Effects of Acetyl-L-Carnitine on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to learn how treatment with acetyl-L-carnitine (ALCAR) will affect the hearts of patients with Friedreich's Ataxia as well as how it may affect other symptoms of Friedreich's Ataxia such as difficulties with balance, walking, or upper arm function.

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of ACTIMMUNE® Dose Escalation in Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this phase 3 randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ACTIMMUNE® (interferon-γ 1b) in the treatment of Friedreich's Ataxia (FA) and to evaluate the pharmacokinetic (PK) characteristics of ACTIMMUNE® in FA patients.

papers.title: A Study of SGT-212 Gene Therapy in Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
This is a phase 1b, first in-human, open-label, dose-finding study investigating the safety and tolerability of SGT-212 in participants with Friedreich's ataxia (FA). It will be delivered via dual intradentate nucleus (IDN) and intravenous (IV) administration to participants with FA.

All participants will receive SGT-212 and will be enrolled in the study for approximately 5 years.

papers.title: Study of LX2006 Gene Therapy in Friedreich Ataxia Cardiomyopathy
papers.summary: The purpose of Study LX2006-03, a multicenter, Phase 2, open-label, randomized, controlled study, is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of LX2006 gene therapy in participants with Friedreich ataxia (FA) cardiomyopathy (CM).

papers.title: A Study to Characterize the Cardiac Phenotype of Individuals With Friedreich's Ataxia (CARFA Study)
papers.summary:
Friedreich's ataxia (FA) is an autosomal recessive disease with an incidence of 1/50,000 in the Caucasian population. The main manifestations of FA are progressive sensory and cerebellar ataxia and cardiomyopathy (CM). It is the most common form of inherited ataxia. A severe CM affects \~60% of FA patients, mostly young adults, and leads to cardiac failure then death. Currently, no therapy can change the course of this severe cardiomyopathy.

This study is designed to characterize the cardiac manifestations of FA using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), echocardiography, serum cardiac biomarker

papers.title: Efficacy, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Multiple Doses of Oral TAK-831 in Adults With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of TAK-831 versus placebo on upper extremity (arm and hands) motor function and manual dexterity. This study will also evaluate the efficacy of TAK-831 versus placebo on activities of daily living (ADL) and other secondary assessments.

papers.title: Single Ascending Dose Study of CTI-1601 Versus Placebo in Subjects With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of single ascending doses of CTI-1601 in participants with Friedreich's ataxia

papers.title: Multiple Ascending Dose Study of CTI-1601 Versus Placebo in Subjects With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of multiple ascending doses of CTI-1601 in participants with Friedreich's ataxia

papers.title: Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Idebenone in the Treatment of Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: This study is meant to assess the effectiveness of idebenone on neurological outcome measures in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia over a 6 months period.

papers.title: Phase 1 Trial of Idebenone to Treat Patients With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
This study will determine the highest amount of idebenone that can be taken without harmful side effects in children, teenagers, and adults with Friedreich's ataxia, a progressive degenerative disease that affects several body systems. Studies in France and Canada showed that patients with Friedreich's ataxia who took idebenone had a decrease in the size of their left ventricle (main pumping chamber of the heart), which is often enlarged in this disease. It is possible that idebenone may also prevent the progression of nervous system degeneration in Friedreich's ataxia.

Patients 5 years of ag

papers.title: Phase IA and IB Study of AAVrh.10hFXN Gene Therapy for the Cardiomyopathy of Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to test the safety and preliminary efficacy of AAVrh.10hFXN to treat the cardiomyopathy associated with Friedreich's ataxia (FA). AAVrh.10hFXN is a serotype rh.10 adeno-associated virus gene transfer vector coding for Frataxin (FXN). The drug is administered intravenously. This is a phase 1, open label, dose escalation study with a total of 25 participants.

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of ACTIMMUNE® Dose Escalation in Friedreich's Ataxia Study
papers.summary: The purpose of this phase 3 multi-center, open-label extension study is to evaluate the long-term safety of ACTIMMUNE® (interferon-γ 1b) in participants with Friedreich's Ataxia.

papers.title: Safety and Pharmacology Study of VP 20629 in Adults With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
The objectives of the study are:

* To evaluate the safety and tolerability of single and multiple oral doses of VP 20629 in subjects with Friedreich's ataxia (FA). \[Primary\]
* To characterize the pharmacokinetics of VP 20629 by investigation of the plasma concentration-time profile following single and multiple oral doses in subjects with FA. \[Secondary\]
* To investigate the pharmacodynamic effects of VP 20629 on plasma 8-isoprostane and malondialdehyde and urinary 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine concentrations following multiple oral doses in subjects with FA. \[Exploratory\]

papers.title: A Study to Assess Nomlabofusp in Adolescents and Children With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of nomlabofusp (CTI-1601) in adolescents and children with Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA).

papers.title: Efficacy of EGb761 in Patients Suffering From Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this protocol is to determine the efficacy of EGb 761 120 mg bid versus placebo in patients suffering from Friedreich Ataxia

papers.title: (+) Epicatechin to Treat Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: This 24-week study will test the safety and effectiveness of synthetically produced (+) Epicatechin in treating patients who have Friedreich's Ataxia, a neurological disorder.

papers.title: Open Trail of γIFN for Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary:
The investigator proposes an open label pilot study to investigate the safety and efficacy of gamma interferon (γIFN) in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia (FRDA). yIFN, an approved drug for treatment of granulomatous disease, has been shown to promote Frataxin expression in FRDA models in vitro and in vivo as well as in pilot human studies.

Safety will monitored by clinical surveillance and biohumoral periodic assessment. Efficacy will be assessed by a combination of advanced neuroimaging techniques and established clinical indicators. The investigators intend to recruit over a 6 months perio

papers.title: A Single Ascending Dose Study of DT-216P2 in Normal Healthy Participants
papers.summary: This purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of single ascending doses of DT-216P2 administered either subcutaneously (SC) and intravenously (IV) in normal healthy participants. Approximately 36 participants will be enrolled into this study.

papers.title: Rosuvastatin (Crestor) in Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: This study is an exploratory open-label clinical trial of Rosuvastatin in patients with Friedreich ataxia (FRDA). This is an outpatient trial with the goal of enrolling 10 evaluable adults with genetically confirmed FRDA who are between the ages of 18-65. Subjects will receive 10mg of oral Rosuvastatin daily for three months.

papers.title: The Use of Assistive Gait Devices Can Reduce the Risk of Falls in Patients With Neuromuscular Diseases Following a Training Period.
papers.summary:
The planned project is an intervention study to assess the risk of falling after adaptation of an assistive gait devices in patients with the following neuromuscular diseases: Inclusion body myositis, myotonic dystrophy, limb girdle and facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophies, Pompe disease, Lambert-Eaton syndrome, myasthenia gravis, spinal muscular atrophy, Guillain-Barré syndrome, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, Friedreich's ataxia and hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy.

The primary aim is to assess the risk of falling after a suitable assistive gait device

papers.title: Pilot Study of Varenicline (Chantix®) in the Treatment of Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine if varenicline is effective in treating symptoms of Friedreich's ataxia.

papers.title: Study to Evaluate DT-216 in Adult Patients With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects of intravenous DT-216 in adult patients with Friedreich Ataxia. This single ascending dose study is randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Effect of Artesunate in Friedreich Ataxia (FA)
papers.summary: This dose-escalation study is aimed at investigating a novel application for artesunate in the treatment of Friedreich ataxia. It will evaluate this novel application of oral artesunate using a surrogate biological marker as primary endpoint in a phase I-II open trial

papers.title: Methylprednisolone Treatment of Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: This study will explore whether methylprednisolone treatment is safe, well-tolerated, and beneficial in patients that are diagnosed with Friedreich Ataxia (FRDA). The study will also explore if methylprednisolone has any effects on biomarkers associated with FRDA. All subjects in the study will receive the same steroid treatment.

papers.title: Idebenone to Treat Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: This study will determine whether a drug called idebenone is safe and effective in reducing the level of oxidants that are believed to damage the nervous system and hearts in patients with Friedreich's ataxia. Friedreich's ataxia is caused by an abnormality in the gene that makes a protein called frataxin, which is necessary for the proper functioning of energy-producing parts of cells called mitrochondria. In Friedreich's ataxia, the mitochondria become overloaded with iron, and high levels of harmful compounds called oxidants are formed. These oxidants are believed to damage the cells of the

papers.title: A Study to Find Out How BIIB141 (Omaveloxolone) is Processed in the Body and to Learn More About Its Safety in Participants With Friedreich's Ataxia Aged 2 to 15 Years Old
papers.summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about BIIB141, also known as omaveloxolone or SKYCLARYS®. This drug has been approved, or made available for doctors to prescribe, for people with Friedrich's Ataxia (FA) who are at least 16 years old. But, it is not yet available for children and teens with FA who are younger than 16 years old. The main goal of this study is to learn how BIIB141 is processed in the body of children and teens who are 2 to 15 years old.

The main question researchers want to answer in this study is:

* How does the body process BIIB141 in children and teens?
* How many

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Subcutaneous Nomlabofusp in Subjects With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous nomlabofusp in adult and pediatric subjects with Friedreich's ataxia

papers.title: Micronised Resveratrol as a Treatment for Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The aim of this study is to assess the efficacy of micronised resveratrol as a treatment for FRDA, in terms of reducing the severity of ataxia symptoms at 24 weeks, through a randomised blinded, placebo controlled crossover trial.

papers.title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effect of MIN-102 on the Progression of Friedreich's Ataxia in Male and Female Patients
papers.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study on the effects of MIN-102 on Biochemical, Imaging, neurophysiological, and clinical markers in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Vatiquinone in Participants With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to assess the long-term safety of vatiquinone in participants with Friedreich ataxia (FA) previously exposed to vatiquinone.

papers.title: A Study of Resveratrol as Treatment for Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the effect of two doses of resveratrol taken for a 12 week period, on frataxin levels in individuals with Friedreich ataxia. This study will also measure the effect of resveratrol on markers of oxidative stress, clinical measures of ataxia, and cardiac parameters.

papers.title: NAD+ Precursor Supplementation in Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The primary objective is to test the safety and tolerability of short-term therapy with a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) precursor (MIB-626) in adults with Friedreich's Ataxia (FA) without overt heart failure and with a left ventricular ejection fraction ≥ 40%. A key secondary objective is to test the effects of MIB-626 on cardiac and skeletal muscle bioenergetics.

papers.title: Electroencephalogram in Patients With Friedreich's Ataxia for the Study of the Structural and Functional Connectome.
papers.summary: Prospective, exploratory, multicenter pilot study investigating the structural and functional connectome in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia (FRDA) using high-density electroencephalogram (HD-EEG). The aim is to identify neurophysiological biomarkers and analyze the relationship between cortical connectivity, cognitive functioning, and clinical severity, particularly in response to rehabilitation treatment.

papers.title: A Study Investigating the Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Deferiprone in Patients With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of deferiprone in subjects with Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA).

The secondary objective is to evaluate the long-term efficacy of deferiprone for the treatment of FRDA.

The tertiary objectives are to evaluate the effect of deferiprone on:

1. cardiac function,
2. quality of life, and
3. functional status.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Etravirine in Friedreich Ataxia Patients
papers.summary: A drug repositioning effort provided evidence supporting the possible use of Etravirine, a drug approved for the treatment of HIV infections in patients starting from 2 years of age, as a treatment for FA. We found that Etravirine is able to increase Frataxin protein both in vitro - in cells derived from FA patients - and in vivo - in the heart and skeletal muscle of Frataxin-deficient YG8 mice. Because of these findings, and since Etravirine displays a generally favorable safety profile, we plan to launch an open-label, phase 2 clinical trial aimed at assessing the safety and efficacy of Etra

papers.title: An Objective Double-blind Evaluation of Bupropion and Citalopram in an Individual With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to document the clinical effects of bupropion and citalopram in a single subject with Friedreich Ataxia.

papers.title: Study to Assess the Safety and Tolerability of Idebenone in the Treatment of Friedreich's Ataxia Patients
papers.summary: This study is meant to assess the safety and tolerability of idebenone in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia over a 12 months period.

papers.title: A Phase IIa Trial to Test Safety and Efficacy Interferon Gamma Treatment in Elevating Frataxin Levels in FRDA Patients
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to investigate whether the treatment with IFN gamma can induce significant accumulation of frataxin in FRDA patients, a possibility suggested by pre-clinical evidence in an animal model of the disease.

papers.title: Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Nicotinamide in Patients With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: Friedreich ataxia is the most frequent early-onset autosomal recessive hereditary ataxia. It is caused by a pathological expansion of a GAA repeat in the first intron of the frataxin gene (FXN) and results in decreased levels of FXN protein. FXN deficiency results in a relentlessly progressive neurodegenerative condition which frequently presents around puberty. Patients gradually lose coordination, become dysarthric and are frequently wheel-chair bound as adolescents. There is no disease modifying therapy and many patients die prematurely of cardiomyopathy. It was subsequently found that the

papers.title: Iron-Chelating Therapy and Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: Friedreich ataxia, an autosomal recessive condition, ascribed to frataxin gene expansion, has been shown to result from an iron- induced injury to the mitochondrial respiratory chain. Buffering free radicals with short-chain quinones (Idebenone) protects the patients against cardiomyopathy but not CNS involvement. Removing CNS iron should limit the impact of the neurological symptoms of the disease.

papers.title: Interferon Gamma-1b in Friedreich Ataxia (FRDA)
papers.summary: Friedreich ataxia (FRDA) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease of children and adults for which there is presently no therapy. Recently, a study reported that interferon gamma (IFN-g) could raise frataxin protein levels in both cell lines derived from patients with Friedreich ataxia and in a mouse model with Friedreich ataxia. The present study will test whether IFN-g is safe, tolerated and potentially efficacious in a heterogeneous cohort of children with FRDA.

papers.title: Effect of Pioglitazone Administered to Patients With Friedreich's Ataxia: Proof of Concept
papers.summary:
Friedreich's ataxia (FA) is a rare progressive neurological disorder affecting approximately 1/30, 000 individuals. No treatment is presently available to counteract the neurodegeneration of this extremely severe disease.

Pioglitazone, a well known PPAR gamma (peroxysome proliferators-activated receptor gamma) ligand induces the expression of many enzymes involved in the mitochondrial metabolism, including the superoxide dismutases. This agent may be therapeutic by counteracting the disabled recruitment of antioxidant enzymes in FA patients. This potential neuroprotective agent crosses the br

papers.title: A Study to Assess Efficacy, Long Term Safety and Tolerability of RT001 in Subjects With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the Efficacy, Long Term Safety and Tolerability of RT001 in subjects with Friedreich's Ataxia

papers.title: Long-Term Safety Extension Study of ACTIMMUNE® (Interferon γ-1b) in Children and Young Adults With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this long term extension study is to evaluate the long-term safety of ACTIMMUNE® (interferon-γ 1b) in participants with Friedreich's Ataxia (FA).

papers.title: Evaluation of the Effects of Calcitriol's in the Neurological Symptoms of Friedreich's Ataxia Patients
papers.summary:
Friedreich's Ataxia (FA) is an autosomal recessive disease the mutation of which leads to a deficiency of a protein called frataxin, which is responsible for the symptoms of the disease. It is assumed that inducing an increase in the production of frataxin could reverse part of the disease's symptoms.

Several treatments with drugs that raise frataxin levels have been tested, but they have either have not given the expected result or have induced intolerable side effects. The IRBLleida (Institut de Recerca Biomèdica de Lleida Fundació Dr. Pifarré) team has shown that calcitriol can increase th

papers.title: A Study to Learn About the Effects and Safety of RTA 408 (Omaveloxolone) in People Aged 16 to 40 With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
In this study, researchers are learning more about RTA 408, also known as omaveloxolone, BIIB141, or SKYCLARYS®. The main goal of this study is to learn more about the safety of RTA 408 and how it affects physical effort, movement, coordination, and how participants feel in daily life.

The main questions researchers want to answer in this study are:

* How much physical effort can a participant produce during a cycling test after 12 weeks of treatment?
* How do scores on the modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale (mFARS) change after 48 weeks?

Researchers will use the modified Friedreich'

papers.title: A Multiple Ascending Dose Study of DT-216P2 in Patients With Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of DT-216P2 administered multiple ascending doses in patients with FA.

papers.title: Study to Evaluate Multiple Ascending Dose and Multi-Dose of DT-216 in Adult Patients With Friedreich Ataxia
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic effects of multiple doses of intravenous DT-216 in adult patients with Friedrich Ataxia.

papers.title: NAD+ and Exercise in FA
papers.summary:
Randomized, placebo-controlled trial with a 2x2 factorial design testing the effects of an NAD+ precursor (NR) and exercise on Peak VO2 and Si in Friedreich's Ataxia (FA).

The primary objective of this research is to measure the effect of combination administration (NR + exercise) on aerobic capacity (Peak VO2) in FA. A key secondary objective is to measure the effect of combination administration (NR + exercise) on glucose homeostasis (Si) in FA.

papers.title: Effect of Nicotinamide in Friedreich's Ataxia
papers.summary:
The purpose of the interventional study is to determine whether Nicotinamide is effective at upregulating the Frataxin (FXN) gene in patients with Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) where this gene is abnormally 'switched off'.

The purpose of the non-interventional study is to investigate the use of novel, highly-sensitive technology to capture clinical deficit and measure subtle changes in the activities of daily living and to correlate functional changes to levels of expression of Frataxin protein and the epigenetic structure of the Frataxin gene over a 9-12 month period without nicotinamide. Healt

papers.title: Long-Term Safety and Tolerability of Idebenone in Friedreich's Ataxia Patients (MICONOS Extension)
papers.summary: This is an Extension study of the MICONOS main randomised placebo-controlled trial (NCT00905268), and open to those patients completing the main study. The scientific aim of this extension study is to monitor safety and tolerability of idebenone over two years in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Friedreich ataxia
Mitochondrial Quality Control in Inherited Mitochondrial Cardiomyopathy: Convergent Pathobiology and a Testable Therapeutic Framework.
papers.summary: This review identifies AAV-mediated FXN gene delivery as a direct strategy for increasing frataxin expression in Friedreich ataxia, with evidence of target engagement in a small early human study and prevention or reversal of cardiomyopathy in a mouse model. Cardiac efficacy and long-term safety remain unconfirmed, and excessive frataxin expression may cause cardiac or hepatic toxicity.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas9-based edition of frataxin gene in Dictyostelium discoideum.
papers.summary: Engineered DdFXN-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum reproduced functional and growth defects associated with frataxin deficiency, while wild-type and G122V DdFXN provided rescue to differing extents. The strain is proposed as a model for screening FA variants and developing therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Partial bypass of frataxin deficiency by ISCU M141I restores cytosolic and nuclear Fe-S cluster assembly.
papers.summary: The study shows that the ISCU M141I variant partially bypasses frataxin deficiency in murine cells by preserving nuclear and cytosolic iron-sulfur protein assembly, while leaving persistent mitochondrial defects and slow proliferation. In Fxn-deficient mice, ISCU M141I delays but does not prevent embryonic lethality, demonstrating incomplete rescue across cellular compartments and in vivo.

papers.title: Partial Bypass of Frataxin Deficiency by ISCU M141I Restores Cytosolic and Nuclear Fe–S Cluster Assembly
papers.summary: The study shows that the ISCU M141I substitution partially bypasses FXN deficiency by preserving cytosolic and nuclear iron-sulfur protein function, improving survival and reducing baseline DNA damage in edited murine fibroblasts. The rescue is incomplete because mitochondrial dysfunction, defective mitochondrial Fe-S proteins, and slower proliferation persist, while embryonic lethality in Fxn-deficient mice is delayed but not fully rescued.

papers.title: Small-molecule inhibitors of proteasome increase CjCas9 protein stability.
papers.summary: Proteasome inhibition with bortezomib stabilized CjCas9 and increased CRISPR-mediated deletion of the intronic GAA repeat region of human FXN in HEK293T cells. The study did not measure or restore FXN gene expression; it measured CjCas9 protein abundance and genomic editing, and proposed this strategy for Friedreich ataxia gene therapy without testing a disease model or patients.

papers.title: Frataxin-Mediated PINK1-Parkin-Dependent Mitophagy in Hepatic Steatosis: The Protective Effects of Quercetin.
papers.summary: In high-fat-diet-fed mice and oleate/palmitate-exposed HepG2 cells, quercetin restored reduced frataxin and enhanced PINK1-Parkin-associated mitophagy, while alleviating hepatic steatosis and lipid accumulation. Frataxin knockdown inhibited this mitophagy pathway and promoted lipid accumulation, while quercetin partially normalized the defect in fatty-acid-exposed knockdown cells.

papers.title: Investigation into the silencing of heterochromatin in mammalian cells
papers.summary: The paper identifies expanded GAA-repeat-associated FXN gene silencing as a mechanism leading to Friedreich’s ataxia and reports that nicotinamide, an HDAC inhibitor, upregulated silenced FXN in treated patients. The upregulated expression was accompanied by reduced heterochromatin histone modification, although the supplied abstract does not report clinical benefit.

papers.title: Histone deacetylases suppress CGG repeat-induced neurodegeneration via transcriptional silencing in models of fragile X tremor ataxia syndrome.
papers.summary: In FXTAS models and patient-derived cells, expanded CGG repeats increase local histone acetylation and FMR1 transcription; HDAC3, HDAC6, or HDAC11 overexpression represses the repeat-containing transgene and suppresses neurodegeneration. Garcinol and anacardic acid reduce FMR1 mRNA and extend lifespan in activated (CGG)90-eGFP flies, but broad chromatin effects, cytotoxicity, and reduced FMRP expression limit their therapeutic utility.

papers.title: Critical roles of IKAROS and HDAC1 in regulation of heterochromatin and tumor suppression in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
papers.summary: This paper shows that IKZF1/IKAROS re-expression restores heterochromatin formation in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia by recruiting HDAC1, enabling EZH2-dependent H3K27me3 formation, repressing active enhancers, and expanding chromatin-repression domains. These chromatin-silencing findings are mechanistically relevant to counteracting FXN gene silencing, although the study does not directly examine FXN, Friedreich ataxia, or chromatin-opening compounds.

papers.title: O-SNAP uncovers nanoscale chromatin remodeling in dedifferentiation and stress responses.
papers.summary: The study shows that O-SNAP can quantify subtle, multiscale chromatin remodeling during chondrocyte dedifferentiation and oxidative stress, including chromatin opening caused by D-alanine/nROS in H3.1-overexpressing cells. It also reports that trichostatin A decompacts chromatin in fibroblasts, but it does not study Friedreich ataxia, FXN, or the specific mechanism “FXN gene silencing,” so transfer of efficacy to Friedreich ataxia remains unproven.

papers.title: Live monitoring uncovers divergent epigenetic remodeling during osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells.
papers.summary: The study developed K9-MILo, a genetically encoded H3K9me3 sensor, and combined long-term live-cell imaging with machine-learning analysis to track heterochromatin remodeling during adipogenic and osteogenic differentiation of ASC52telo mesenchymal stem cells. Indomethacin increased lipid-droplet formation without measurably changing the global H3K9me3 remodeling trajectory, but the assay does not provide locus-specific information such as the status of individual gene promoters; the paper does not study Friedreich ataxia or FXN gene silencing.

papers.title: ARID1A Mediates SWI/SNF-Independent Maintenance of Heterochromatin Architecture to Restrain Viral Mimicry and Immunogenicity in Colon Cancer.
papers.summary: This study shows that ARID1A maintains heterochromatin architecture through a TRIM28-associated complex that represses endogenous retroelements, thereby limiting viral mimicry and type I interferon-mediated immunogenicity in colorectal cancer. Disrupting the ARID1A-TRIM28 interaction with synthetic peptides induced viral mimicry and T-cell infiltration in ARID1A wild-type tumors and suppressed tumor growth, while also increasing sensitivity to PD-1 blockade.

papers.title: Ferroptosis inhibitor improves cardiac function more effectively than inhibitors of apoptosis and necroptosis through cardiac mitochondrial protection in rats with iron-overloaded cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: In a male Wistar rat model of iron overload cardiomyopathy, the ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 and the iron chelator deferoxamine restored cardiac function, while apoptosis and necroptosis inhibitors produced only partial improvement. The study identifies ferroptosis as the predominant form of cardiomyocyte death and associates its inhibition with reduced mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: Biallelic FDXR mutations induce ferroptosis in a rare mitochondrial disease with ataxia.
papers.summary: The paper reports a patient with biallelic FDXR mutations and an FDXR-associated mitochondrial disease characterized by optic atrophy, ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, mitochondrial abnormalities, iron overload, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and dysregulated glutathione peroxidase-4. Deferoxamine, N-acetyl-cysteine, and ferrostatin-1 reduced oxidative stress and cell death in patient-derived lymphoblastic cell lines, while idebenone showed protective effects against cellular injuries induced by FDXR mutations.

papers.title: Iron accumulates in Huntington's disease neurons: protection by deferoxamine.
papers.summary: The paper identifies redox-active ferrous iron accumulation in perinuclear, membrane-bound structures of striatal neurons in R6/2 Huntington’s disease mice and links it to a compensatory alteration of neuronal iron-homeostasis proteins. Intraventricular deferoxamine improved motor performance and reduced treated-side ventricular enlargement, providing preclinical evidence that lowering neuronal iron can protect against Huntington’s disease phenotypes.

papers.title: Ferroptosis contributes to boar sperm deterioration during liquid semen storage.
papers.summary: The study shows that ferroptosis is experimentally inducible and pharmacologically modifiable in boar sperm during liquid storage, with Ferrostatin-1 and N-acetylcysteine providing partial protection against oxidative injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, membrane damage, and motility loss. It reports increased intracellular labile Fe2+ accumulation, but does not specifically demonstrate mitochondrial iron accumulation or test transfer to Friedreich ataxia.

papers.title: Mex-3 RNA-binding family member A limits macrophage ferroptosis-associated injury linked to the SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway in diabetic atherosclerosis.
papers.summary: In diabetic atherosclerotic mice and stressed macrophages, MEX3A deficiency increased iron-linked redox stress, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis-associated injury, while GPX4 or SLC7A11 overexpression reduced intracellular Fe2+ accumulation and oxidative injury. Ferrostatin-1 partially suppressed macrophage lipid peroxidation and improved plaque destabilization, but the study measured labile intracellular Fe2+ rather than directly demonstrating mitochondrial iron accumulation.

papers.title: Dysregulation of iron protein expression in the G93A model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.summary: In differentiated G93A-SOD1 SH-SY5Y cells modeling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, iron-related gene expression, total iron content, and reactive oxygen species were increased, consistent with increased iron uptake and mitochondrial iron import. The study suggests that reactive oxygen species mediate an IRE/IRP-independent increase in mitochondrial iron-handling genes, but it did not directly quantify mitochondrial iron accumulation or demonstrate therapeutic rescue.

papers.title: A near-infrared fluorescent probe for dynamic HClO monitoring in epilepsy and high-throughput discovery of natural neuroprotectants.
papers.summary: The paper developed MB-Mito, a mitochondria-targeted, blood-brain-barrier-permeable fluorescent probe for monitoring hypochlorous acid and screening antioxidants in epilepsy models. Myricetin reduced mitochondrial hypochlorous acid accumulation, oxidative injury, apoptosis, and neuronal damage while increasing ERK/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling in kainic-acid-induced cellular and mouse models.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Effects of 3,6-Dihydroxyflavone in LPS-Stimulated BV-2 Microglial Cells and an MPTP-Induced Mouse Model of Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In an MPTP-induced mouse model of Parkinson's disease, 3,6-dihydroxyflavone (3,6-DHF) increased Nrf2 and HO-1 protein expression in the substantia nigra pars compacta and striatum, while reducing lipid peroxidation and restoring antioxidant defenses. In parallel, 3,6-DHF reduced motor deficits, dopaminergic neuronal loss, and neuroinflammatory markers; these findings provide a mechanistically relevant Nrf2/HO-1 intervention for further investigation, but no transfer to Friedreich ataxia or human clinical efficacy was tested.

papers.title: TFEB-dependent autophagy-lysosomal pathway is required for NRF2-driven antioxidative action in obstructive sleep apnea-induced neuronal injury.
papers.summary: In obstructive sleep apnea mouse models, defective TFEB-dependent autophagy-lysosomal pathway activity and impaired NRF2 induction are associated with oxidative stress, hippocampal neuronal death, and cognitive impairment. Enhancing NRF2 restores neuronal redox balance and protects hippocampal neurons, while NRF2 and TFEB pathway manipulations show bidirectional regulatory interdependence.

papers.title: Liposomes-Loaded miR-9-5p Alleviated Hypoxia-Ischemia-Induced Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress by Targeting ZBTB20 to Inhibiting Nrf2/Keap1 Interaction in Neonatal Mice.
papers.summary: The paper reports that liposome-delivered miR-9-5p reduces hypoxia-ischemia-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress in neonatal mice and H2O2-exposed PC12 cells. The protective effect is associated with ZBTB20 regulation, Nrf2/Keap1 signaling, improved mitochondrial function, and antioxidant-protein expression; ML385 reverses these protective effects.

papers.title: Targeting Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress to Protect Against Preterm Birth and Fetal Brain Injury via Nrf2 Induction.
papers.summary: This study shows that the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO ameliorated oxidative stress and inflammation in an LPS-induced preterm birth mouse model, improved placental function, and reduced fetal brain injury and long-term neurodevelopmental impairments. In trophoblast cells, MitoTEMPO promoted Keap1 degradation and Nrf2 activation, and Nrf2 inhibition demonstrated that its anti-inflammatory and protective effects depend on Nrf2/ARE signaling.

papers.title: Activation of the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 pathway by cGAMP Mitigates oxidative stress and ferroptosis in ischaemic stroke.
papers.summary: The paper reports that cGAMP activates the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 pathway in a mouse model of transient focal cerebral ischemia, reducing brain lesion size, improving neurobehavioral outcomes, limiting mitochondrial oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation, and preserving mitochondrial cristae. Pharmacological inhibition of Nrf2 with ML-385 or GPX4 with ML-210 completely abolished these protective effects.

papers.title: CAPNS1 restoration partially alleviates mitochondrial dysfunction and synaptic deficits in Alzheimer's disease through the Ca<sup>2+</sup>-CaMKIIβ-MAPK-PGC-1α axis.
papers.summary: This paper reports that CAPNS1 restoration activates a Ca²⁺-CaMKIIβ-MAPK-PGC-1α pathway associated with mitochondrial biogenesis and respiratory capacity, restoring cellular ATP production while reducing mitochondrial reactive oxygen species in Alzheimer’s disease models. Neuronal CAPNS1 upregulation in APP/PS1 mice improved mitochondrial cristae, hippocampal long-term potentiation, dendritic spine density, and spatial memory, but the proposed pathway and therapeutic relevance remain uncertain because loss-of-function experiments and direct validation of mitochondrial biogenesis were not performed.

papers.title: Sestrin2 Silencing Exacerbates Cerebral Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury by Decreasing Mitochondrial Biogenesis through the AMPK/PGC-1α Pathway in Rats.
papers.summary: In a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model, Sesn2 silencing reduced AMPK/PGC-1α signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis markers, antioxidant proteins, and worsened neurological, infarct, oxidative-stress, and neuronal outcomes. The AMPK activator AICAR largely restored signaling and mitochondrial biogenesis-related protein expression and improved neurological and ischemic outcomes, supporting AMPK/PGC-1α-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis as a transferable therapeutic mechanism for mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress.

papers.title: Metformin inhibits methylglyoxal-induced retinal pigment epithelial cell death and retinopathy via AMPK-dependent mechanisms: Reversing mitochondrial dysfunction and upregulating glyoxalase 1.
papers.summary: The paper shows that methylglyoxal suppresses AMPK-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis in retinal pigment epithelial cells, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death, while metformin and A769662 reverse these effects. Metformin also protects mouse retina from methylglyoxal-induced retinopathy, although it does not restore methylglyoxal-inhibited mitochondrial respiration in ARPE-19 cells.

papers.title: Metformin protects high glucose‑cultured cardiomyocytes from oxidative stress by promoting NDUFA13 expression and mitochondrial biogenesis via the AMPK signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In high-glucose-cultured H9C2 cardiomyocytes, metformin protected cells from oxidative injury while increasing mitochondrial gene expression and mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors. AMPK inhibition with Compound C blocked metformin-induced NDUFA13 expression and the mitochondrial biogenesis response, providing a transferable experimental precedent, although the evidence is limited to one cell line and pharmacologic AMPK inhibition.

papers.title: Anomalous AMPK-regulated angiotensin AT1R expression and SIRT1-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis at RVLM in hypertension programming of offspring to maternal high fructose exposure.
papers.summary: In a rat model of maternal high-fructose-exposure–programmed hypertension, impaired AMPK/SIRT1 signaling reduced SIRT1-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis in the rostral ventrolateral medulla, lowered mitochondrial DNA copy number and ATP content, and was associated with oxidative stress, sympathoexcitation, and hypertension. Metformin and simvastatin restored markers of mitochondrial biogenesis and improved measured outcomes, while losartan improved oxidative and cardiovascular outcomes without correcting AMPK/SIRT1 suppression.

papers.title: Herba Houttuyniae Extract Benefits Hyperlipidemic Mice via Activation of the AMPK/PGC-1α/Nrf2 Cascade.
papers.summary: In acute poloxamer 407-induced hyperlipidemia in mice, liver and heart tissues showed reduced AMPK activity, PGC-1α expression, mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers, mitochondrial complex activity, mtDNA copy number or ATP production. Herba houttuyniae aqueous extract (HAE), particularly at 200 mg/kg/day, restored AMPK signaling, increased mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers and function, reduced oxidative stress, and improved some hepatic and cardiac abnormalities; some measures, including cardiac ventricular dimensions and selected mitochondrial markers, were not restored.
